We need to propose a retrosynthesis route up to 5 steps, leaves must be commercially available chemicals, total price <= $9999 (we cannot check price but assume buyable). Need to construct JSON tree.

We have target SMILES: O[C@H]1C[C@@H](O[C@@H]([C@@H]1C)/C=C(CO)/C)C/C=C/C=C/C(O)=O

We have applied template 1037371 gave precursor: "C/C(=C/[C@H]1O[C@@H](C/C=C/C=C/C(=O)O)C[C@H](OC(=O)/C=C/C=C/C=C/C=C/C(=O)O)[C@H]1C)CO"

That seems to be a molecule with two ester groups? Actually product is target; reactant is a molecule with an ester? The template seems to break an ester to give alcohol? Wait retro template: [C:3]-[C:2](-[C:4])-[OH]>> O-C(=O)/... So applying to target gave a precursor that is a di-ester? The result is a single SMILES (maybe a precursor with two ester groups). That precursor may be further disassembled.

We need to find commercially available leaves. Likely we can break down to simpler fragments like cinnamic acid derivatives, etc.

Maybe we can propose a route: target -> precursor A (via ester hydrolysis? Actually reverse). Then break that precursor into two fragments using another template (maybe cleavage of ester to give acid and alcohol). Use template 42530 gave precursor: "C/C(=C/[C@H]1O[C@@H](C/C=C/C=C/C(=N)O)C[C@H](O)[C@H]1C)CO" and O (water). That precursor is similar but with amide? Actually contains C(=N)O (carboxamide). That may be further broken.

We need to ensure leaves are buyable. Let's check buyability of that precursor.
